assessment: Unused aggregate room-hours coexist with unmet requests, but usable alternatives and equipment needs are unknown. A combined allocation-and-confirmation mechanism is plausible; neither feasibility nor attainment of the eight-week targets follows from the observations.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: combine equipment-and-window-aware reservation exchange with a single committed booking revision checked at key collection. The named interface is the handoff from a proposed multi-group exchange to confirmed room-access rights. Obtain every affected group's consent by telephone or in person before committing the whole exchange; until then, existing reservations remain valid.
openings.delta: Acceptable-window matching could expose exchanges hidden by inherited bookings, while coordinated confirmation could make those exchanges dependable. Matching alone can increase conflicting expectations; a reliable ledger alone cannot discover better allocations. Together they may turn nominal spare capacity into usable rehearsal access without adding volunteer reconciliation work.
openings.prediction: If compatible exchanges exist, the combined mechanism will meet more stated needs than confirmation alone and produce fewer inconsistent room-access expectations than exchange planning alone. Exchanges must preserve every requesting group's weekly 60-minute entitlement, equipment suitability, staffed hours and both booked performances; actual rehearsal needs may exceed the entitlement.
openings.probe: Use the short contact conversations to record total needs, acceptable windows and equipment. Replay the same requests under four conditions: current booking practice, matching only, committed revisions only, and both. Count fully met needs and simulate a change arriving between calendar copying and key collection; count contradictory authorizations and volunteer minutes. Trial only consented, constraint-preserving exchanges, using the desk record as authority and revision-marked calendar copies. Over eight weeks test the stated 90% needs, fewer-than-two-conflicts and two-hours-per-week targets. If no feasible exchange emerges, reject the allocation-benefit hypothesis.
assumptions: Some groups have acceptable alternatives and consent to exchanges.
The staffed desk can maintain one authoritative record and communicate committed changes through existing channels.
Protecting weekly entitlement is feasible within the supplied capacity; the mechanism cannot resolve an infeasible demand pattern.
